newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off on Dow, earnings, data fears.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off on Dow, earnings, data fears.

text.p: Mexican stocks recovered from an early slide on the back of the Dow Jones on Monday, but still closed lower in cautious trade while awaiting economic data and first-quarter earnings reports, traders said.
"We basically followed the Dow (Jones)," a desk trader said. "Dealing was slow, they're apprehensive over first quarter reports, and this week also sees trade balance and inflation data."
The leading IPC share index was down 29.89 points, or 0.79 percent, at 3,758.54. Trading volume was lackluster at 58.99 million shares.
"The market opened with stocks on offer because of nervousness over recent central bank intervention in the secondary market," another desk trader said.
"Then things looked like improving when the market began to forecast cuts in primary interest rates, but then the Dow sagged and took us with it," he added.
The Dow Jones closed down 43.34 points at 6,660.21, up from a low of 6,616.86 points.
In a parallel move, the IPC partially recovered from a session low of 3,750.99 points.
Banco de Mexico recently modified the way it participates in the secondary money market, using repos as its main tool for draining liquidity.
Traders said the operational shift prompted high secondary rates which augured further gains in primary rates.

Dealers said forthcoming inflation data were crucial to determining whether the central bank could cut interest rates. A Reuters survey of Mexico City financial houses MXAAP predicted an average increase in consumer prices of 0.64 percent for April 1-15.
Financial stock GFB, off four centavos to 2.72 pesos, was the most traded stock of the session and weighed most on the downside.
"First quarter reports for financial stocks in general don't look like being so good," said one trader. "Look at Banacci, they hit it hard."
Banacci B shares fell 50 centavos to 16.98 and ended near the head of the prominent decliners' list.
Another trader said financial stocks were also fundamentally weak.
"No one is recommending financials right now, they have no near-term growth prospects," he said.

Telecomms firm Telmex, off 28 centavos to 16.20 pesos, also weighed heavily on the downside. Dealers said Telmex was paring sharp gains it made last week, and fell in tandem with its ADR, which fell 3/4 to 41.
Telmex L and GFB B shares accounted for 42 percent of all shares traded during the session.
Traders noted that retail stock Cifra, up 38 centavos to 11.68 pesos, was the most heavily traded gainer, boosted by an improved earnings outlook.
"Cifra won't post a wonderful report, but at the least the slump looks like stopping," a trader said, referring to a slowdown in retail sales since the peso devaluation crisis of December 1994.
On the broad market, a total of 103 stocks were traded, of which sliders outnumbered gainers by 48 tpo 26.
(( --Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 729-7907))
